title: A case study of successful leadership by an elementary school principal in Japan
text_snippet: A case study of successful leadership by an elementary school principal in Japan Purpose This study aims to explore the characteristics and strategies of successful school leadership in a specific school in Japan, focusing on leadership values, identity and practices, and how stakeholders within and across the education system, including the principal, teachers, students, parents and community members, perceive successful school leadership in the context. Design/methodology/approach This study utilised a multi-perspective single case study approach using individual and focus group interviews with a principal, teachers, students, parents and community members, as well as a survey of the principal and teachers in an urban Japanese school. The interview and survey questions follow the International Successful School Principalship Project (ISSPP) protocol. Interviews were conducted using semi-structured interviews. Discourse analysis was adopted for the qualitative data. The quantitative survey data were used to complement the qualitative analysis. title: Fostering teacher commitment through inclusive leadership: the mediating roles of teacher collaboration and teacher professionalism
text_snippet: Fostering teacher commitment through inclusive leadership: the mediating roles of teacher collaboration and teacher professionalism Purpose This study examines the impact of inclusive leadership on teacher commitment by investigating the mediating roles of teacher collaboration and professionalism. Design/methodology/approach The study employed a cross-sectional survey method, and participants were selected using a convenience sampling technique. The proposed model was tested using structural equation modeling to analyze the direct and indirect relationships between variables. Findings The findings indicate that inclusive leadership positively influences teacher commitment, both directly and indirectly, through teacher collaboration and professionalism. Teacher professionalism emerged as a stronger mediator than collaboration. Originality/value This study provides new insights that inclusive leadership is crucial in strengthening teacher commitment, particularly when it fosters collaborative and professional environments. Additionally, the study highlights contextual differences, as the impact of inclusive leadership on teacher professionalism may be more pronounced in centralized education systems like Türkiye.

title: Boosting novice teachers’ retention intention: international evidence on the role of mentoring via job satisfaction and organizational commitment
text_snippet: Boosting novice teachers’ retention intention: international evidence on the role of mentoring via job satisfaction and organizational commitment Purpose This study aims to provide international evidence on the effectiveness of mentoring programs in increasing new teachers’ expected career length, focusing on the mediating roles of job satisfaction and organizational commitment. Design/methodology/approach This study utilizes multilevel structural equation modeling to analyze international data from the Teaching and Learning International Survey 2018. Findings The results indicate a direct effect of mentoring program participation on novice teachers’ expected career length. The study reveals that this relationship is mediated by organizational commitment, while job satisfaction does not serve as a mediating factor. These findings deepen our understanding of the mechanisms through which mentoring programs relate to novice teachers’ expected career length. Practical implications School leaders and policymakers are encouraged to provide and tailor mentoring programs in a way to promote organizational commitment, thereby enhancing the effectiveness of mentoring on novice teachers’ retention. title: Collaboration, connections and confidence: the influence of school structures on new teacher sense of belonging
text_snippet: Collaboration, connections and confidence: the influence of school structures on new teacher sense of belonging Purpose Organizational scholars note workplace sense of belonging can increase job satisfaction and employee retention. However, we know little about how K-12 schools and districts can support the development of a sense of belonging among their educators. The purpose of this study is to understand how teachers’ sense of belonging is shaped by the organizational features of a school. Design/methodology/approach We used a qualitative interview-based research design where we interviewed 39 teachers in their first 5 years of teaching in one elementary school district and employed inductive qualitative coding methods to understand the organizational influences on educators’ sense of belonging at school. Findings Findings suggest that belonging is enhanced when organizational features (policies and practices that link people, resources and tasks) (1) support collaboration and feeling included, (2) lift educator voice and build connections and (3) enhance confidence. Importantly, the presence of specific organizational features was not enough. What mattered was how educators experienced them. title: Superintendent voices: the impact of gender and race while seeking and serving in the superintendency
text_snippet: Superintendent voices: the impact of gender and race while seeking and serving in the superintendency Purpose This qualitative study explores how gender and race impacted superintendents as they sought a superintendent position as well as how gender and race impact superintendents while serving in the role of superintendent in North Carolina. Design/methodology/approach This phenomenological study is part of a larger study aimed to investigate the current state of the NC superintendency by giving voice to individual and collective experiences of our school superintendents. We used semi-structured interviews with a sample size of 18 current or recently departed superintendents. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis. Findings Five themes were identified: gender bias including White male advantage, racial bias including stereotyping and higher expectations for Black superintendents, biases based on the intersectionality of gender and race for Black women superintendents, the impact of school board positionality, and the value of being coached or mentored. Findings highlight how many White male superintendents in NC are keenly aware of how their identity advanced their pathways and gave them “seats at tables” when Black and/or women leaders did not report those same privileges. title: Instructional leadership as a catalyst for teacher professionalism: a multilevel mediation model of teacher collaboration
text_snippet: Instructional leadership as a catalyst for teacher professionalism: a multilevel mediation model of teacher collaboration Purpose This study tested the effects of instructional leadership on teacher collaboration and professionalism. Specifically, it focused on how teacher collaboration mediates this relationship. Design/methodology/approach A multilevel structural equation model was employed, utilizing data collected from 401 teachers in Türkiye and analyzed. Findings The findings reveal that neither gender nor seniority predicts teacher professionalism at the teacher level. However, at the school level, the findings demonstrate that instructional leadership affects teacher collaboration and teacher collaboration affects teacher professionalism. Moreover, teacher collaboration mediates the relationship between instructional leadership and teacher professionalism. Research limitations/implications The research advances understanding of how instructional leadership affects teacher professionalism through collaboration, an area underexplored in existing literature. Methodologically, the study leverages a multilevel approach that accounts for individual and contextual factors, offering a more nuanced analysis of nested data. title: Distributed leadership strengthening the role of transformational leadership in enhancing teacher psychological capital and well-being
text_snippet: Distributed leadership strengthening the role of transformational leadership in enhancing teacher psychological capital and well-being Purpose This study explored the mediating role of psychological capital and the moderating role of distributed leadership in the relationship between principals’ transformational leadership and teachers’ well-being to understand how integrating distributed and transformational leadership could enhance teacher psychological capital and well-being. Design/methodology/approach A multilevel moderated mediation analysis was conducted using the data collected from 994 teachers across 70 schools in Türkiye. Findings We found a positive relationship between transformational leadership and teacher psychological capital, which was then related to teacher well-being, indicating an indirect relationship through psychological capital. Distributed leadership significantly moderated the direct relationship between transformational leadership and teacher psychological capital and the indirect relationship between transformational leadership and teacher well-being through psychological capital. title: Social justice school leadership through the century (1904–2020): from foundations to anomalies
text_snippet: Social justice school leadership through the century (1904–2020): from foundations to anomalies Purpose This study examines social justice school leadership (SJSL) historical progression across 120 years (1900–2020s) using Kuhn’s structure of scientific revolutions framework. Design/methodology/approach We analyzed citation network and co-citation network from 177 peer-reviewed SJSL articles. Main path analysis was conducted to identify growth trajectories in the citation network. Co-citation network analysis was conducted to examine the intellectual landscape and evolution of influential works. Findings Main path analysis illuminates multiple growth trajectories that have progressed from transformative frameworks in leadership preparation to broader applications in diverse educational settings. The results of co-citation network analysis suggest four interconnected sub-areas: (1) educational leadership preparation through transformative frameworks and andragogy, (2) social justice leadership theory and practices, (3) qualitative methods, and (4) critical race theory. Moreover, influential works evolved from moral principles in the 1900s to critical pedagogy focused on social justice and equity in the 2010s. title: District-level inclusive leadership: leveraging legal compliance as a mechanism to propel inclusive education
text_snippet: District-level inclusive leadership: leveraging legal compliance as a mechanism to propel inclusive education Purpose The purpose was to examine actions administrators make as they are in charge of special education that aims to cultivate inclusive education. Design/methodology/approach Qualitative research methodology with phenomenological in-depth interviewing was used to understand perspectives of seven district-level special education administrators. Findings Results indicate participants aligned leadership to legal compliance as a tactic to justify, combat opposition, and extend inclusion. Originality/value This research contributes to the scant body of literature on educational administration needed to cultivate inclusive districts.

title: “A world of trans vibrance and trans liberation”: how schools support trans educators
text_snippet: “A world of trans vibrance and trans liberation”: how schools support trans educators Purpose Research indicates that trans people are at a high risk of experiencing harm in school environments. At the same time, scholars and activists have urged for a renewed focus on “trans joy” in the face of increasing transphobic backlash to humanize and present more positive narratives of trans life. Drawing upon three case studies of trans educators who felt supported in their transness in their schools, this paper describes how school leaders, peers and structures contributed to positive workplace experiences for trans school workers. We also discuss how these factors influence employment decisions. Design/methodology/approach We use close reading and flexible coding to analyse three in-depth interviews representing outlier cases from a more extensive mixed-methods study with trans school workers in Canada and the United States about their working conditions, job satisfaction and well-being. These cases were chosen because participants described overwhelmingly positive experiences in locations, policy contexts or types of schools we did not anticipate would likely support such experiences. title: Leading through a crisis: caring, supportive, and social justice leadership of school principals in Israel’s minority Arab society
text_snippet: Leading through a crisis: caring, supportive, and social justice leadership of school principals in Israel’s minority Arab society Purpose To explore how Arab school principals in Israel perceived and enacted their leadership roles during the COVID-19 pandemic. Design/methodology/approach This exploratory qualitative study employed semi-structured interviews to evaluate the perspectives of 46 principals overseeing Arab public elementary, middle and high schools in Israel. Findings Three key themes were revealed: caring leadership (emotional well-being, mental health and relational trust), supportive leadership (practical, emotional and resource-based support) and social justice leadership (community aid, socioeconomic support and ensuring teacher and student safety). Practical implications Ongoing training for principals in emotional intelligence and crisis leadership and management, alongside structured support for teachers, will enhance resilience and effectiveness in schools, particularly in low socioeconomic contexts, facing future unexpected crises. title: Agents of change? How district leaders shape absorptive capacity within research–practice partnerships
text_snippet: Agents of change? How district leaders shape absorptive capacity within research–practice partnerships Purpose This study explores how district leaders shape the absorptive capacity of research–practice partnerships (RPPs) when addressing local problems of practice. Design/methodology/approach Drawing from Farrell et al. (2019), we focus on three core partnership domains shaping absorptive capacity: (a) prior knowledge, (b) communication pathways and (c) strategic knowledge leadership. We then employ a mixed-methods, multiple-case study design (Yin, 2013), highlighting two districts participating in a five-year National Science Foundation grant (2019–2024) to improve math instruction and learning. Data collected include semi-structured interviews ( N = 180), the Visions of High-Quality Mathematics Instruction Rubric (VHQMI), social network surveys, meeting observations ( N = 80) and the effective teams rubric (ETR). Findings Data suggest that district leaders variably shape an RPP’s absorptive capacity to engage in joint-partnership work. Notably, these differences are related to the degree to which district leaders promote or hinder the assimilation of new knowledge among other stakeholders within the RPP network. title: Illustrating the power and complexity of a National Longitudinal Superintendent Database through an exploration of cross-state mobility
text_snippet: Illustrating the power and complexity of a National Longitudinal Superintendent Database through an exploration of cross-state mobility Purpose This paper has three purposes: (1) to underscore the importance of compiling comprehensive data on superintendents, (2) to describe the creation of the National Longitudinal Superintendent Database (NLSD) and (3) to illustrate the value of sustained investment in national longitudinal data by analyzing cross-state superintendent attrition and mobility. Design/methodology/approach We present descriptive and correlational analyses of the nuances and nature of cross-state superintendent mobility that demonstrate the distinct knowledge-building opportunities afforded by the establishment of an NLSD. We then build on our description of the establishment of the NLSD to discuss the strengths and challenges of developing and sustaining a national superintendent database that incorporates both qualitative and quantitative data and provide recommendations for a path forward to expand the accuracy of and access to superintendent data. Findings Our findings suggest that superintendent cross-state mobility is higher than that of other educators and that racial and gender inequities persist in these leadership pathways. title: A critical review of cross-cultural adaptation and psychometric validation studies of the principal instructional management rating scale (PIMRS)
text_snippet: A critical review of cross-cultural adaptation and psychometric validation studies of the principal instructional management rating scale (PIMRS) Purpose Despite the widespread international use of the Principal Instructional Management Rating Scale (PIMRS), limited contemporary attention has focused on its adaptation across cultural contexts and the breadth of validation evidence supporting those adaptations. Design/methodology/approach This integrative review examined 12 formal PIMRS adaptation and validation studies conducted across nine countries. The included studies were classified as validation-only, adaptation and validation, or reconstruction and validation, and critically examined for model retention or modification, contextual adaptation, sampling characteristics, and psychometric evidence. Findings Consistent retention of the three-dimensional PIMRS framework across the 12 reviewed studies offers preliminary evidence of conceptual stability alongside localized modification across cultural and institutional settings. Selective modification or removal of functions such as Curriculum Coordination, Principal Visibility, and Incentives for Learning highlights the need for contextual sensitivity in adapting the instrument.
